clues.title: Smudges
text: In southern and eastern North Macedonia, some roads have recognizable smudges on the camera: A large dead insect on the R1205, a vertical pattern of about four smudges on the PS27, a central smudge (plus more further south) on the easternmost part of the A3, a brown smudge on the lower left center in the southeast of the country, and on the A1 to Bitola, a single smudge higher up to the left with a short section of two brown smudges center left halfway between Bitola and Prilep

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: North Macedonia uses two types of bollards.
One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped.
They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.
Croatia uses the same wedge-shaped bollard.
Hungary has a similar wedge-shaped bollard but with more white space above the black rectangle.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 No Antenna
text: All coverage in North Macedonia is Generation 3.
There will never be an antenna on the Google car.
Every other country in Europe will sometimes or always have an antenna in Generation 3 coverage.
The only other country to have no antenna the majority of the time is Serbia, although there will be an antenna sometimes.

clues.title: Plate: North Macedonia
text: North Macedonian licence plates are white and sometimes have the standard European blue strip on the left. They also have a noticeable red block near the left side of the licence plate.
NOTE: Serbia will almost always have a blue strip on their licence plates.

clues.title: Language: Macedonian
text: Macedonian is a South Slavic language closely related to Bulgarian. Macedonian uses the Cyrillic script. Road signs have Latin on them too, although most other signs are fully in Cyrillic.

The letters **Ѓ** and **Ќ** are unique to Macedonian. **Љ**, **Њ**, and **Џ** are only used in Serbo-Croatian and Macedonian (not in Bulgarian). The same goes for the letter **J** (loaned from Latin), where **Й** is used in Bulgarian instead. Bulgarian uses the letter **Ъ** which is not found in Macedonian or Serbo-Croatian.
The Macedonian word for street is **улица** (ulitsa), like most Slavic languages.
